claims.text: As-cast equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a single-phase simple solid solution.
The starting alloy has favorable plasticity and machinability.
The starting alloy has relatively low hardness and strength.
The low hardness and strength are governed by easy dislocation glide combined with rapid dynamic recovery.
The single-phase starting material lacks significant secondary-phase or precipitate barriers to dislocation motion.
Dislocations generated under load can move readily in the starting material.
Dislocations generated under load annihilate readily through dynamic recovery.
Dynamic recovery limits the accumulation of dislocation density.
Limited dislocation accumulation causes low work hardening.
Easy glide occurs along multiple slip systems in this alloy.
Easy glide along multiple slip systems produces a high rate of dislocation annihilation.
Rapid quenching after deformation suppresses dynamic recovery and freezes a higher dislocation density into the alloy.
Slow cooling or annealing after deformation permits greater recovery and maintains standard dislocation-annihilation behavior.
A higher retained dislocation density creates stronger barriers to subsequent dislocation motion.
Rapidly quenched, deformed samples will have higher hardness than the baseline or slowly cooled samples.
Rapidly quenched, deformed samples will have higher yield strength than the baseline or slowly cooled samples.
Rapidly quenched, deformed samples will exhibit a higher work-hardening rate.

The proposed mechanism applies specifically to single-phase equimolar CoCrFeNiTi under ambient loading and may not apply when secondary phases, precipitates, or elevated-temperature deformation mechanisms are present.

contradictions.description: The proposed cause is dynamic recovery occurring under load during room-temperature deformation, but the intervention intended to suppress it is rapid quenching only after deformation. A post-deformation quench cannot prevent recovery that has already occurred during deformation, so the intervention does not directly manipulate the stated governing process.
